# Results — Study 369 (Earnings-Revision-Momentum)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **stocks
whose earnings estimates are being revised up keep beating the market** (the analyst-revision
/ post-earnings-announcement-drift factor) — tested on a **transparent revision proxy**. Paid
analyst-revision feeds (IBES) are not free on yfinance, so we proxy "up-revision" with each
stock's realized **earnings surprise** (reported EPS beats the consensus estimate) plus the
**q/q change in the consensus estimate**. Each earnings quarter we rank a fixed basket by this
revision score, go **long the top tercile / short the bottom tercile**, hold ~a quarter, and
measure each leg's return **in excess of SPY**. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance — daily adjusted closes (SPY + 40-name basket) **and** per-quarter EPS estimate / reported / surprise (`get_earnings_dates`), public, no key |
| Earnings window | 2001-09-26 → 2026-06-10 (**3,847** earnings events, **39** names, ~99 quarters each) |
| Price window | 1995-01-03 → 2026-06-22 (entry/exit prices for the forward-return legs) |
| Revision proxy | z(realized surprise) + z(q/q estimate change), cross-sectional per earnings quarter; **PROXY** for an IBES up-revision flag |
| Book | long top tercile / short bottom tercile of `rev_score`; equal-weight, excess-of-SPY |
| Entry / costs | 1-day execution lag; one-way **10 bps/leg** (4 crossings/rebalance) + **50 bps/yr** borrow on the short leg |

> **Proxy + survivorship caveat (named on the Signal axis).** A *realized* surprise + a
> q/q estimate change is a **noisier, lagged** stand-in for a live analyst-revision feed, and a
> fixed surviving-names basket excludes the firms whose estimates cratered into delisting — a
> mild upward tilt on the long leg and a *missing* tail on the short leg. The verdict does not
> hinge on the proxy's exact construction: it hinges on the fact that the long-short spread is
> statistically indistinguishable from a label-shuffle at the canonical quarterly horizon and
> **negative net of costs** — and survivorship can only *flatter* the result we report.

## The signal — long-short tercile spread (excess of SPY) by holding horizon

1-day entry lag; the spread is the per-quarter (top − bottom) mean excess return. The Welch *t*
is the one-sample *t* of the per-quarter spread vs zero; the placebo *p* is the share of 10,000
within-quarter **label shuffles** whose mean spread matches/beats the real book.

| horizon | n events | n quarters | long ex. | short ex. | **spread** | Welch *t* | placebo *p* | long-leg hit-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month (21d)  | 3,842 | 99 | +0.41% | +0.17% | **+0.25%** | 0.97 | 0.135 | 50% |
| **1-quarter (63d)** | 3,808 | 98 | +0.58% | +0.37% | **+0.21%** | **0.42** | 0.304 | 50% |
| 2-quarter (126d) | 3,769 | 97 | +1.99% | +0.54% | **+1.45%** | **1.98** | 0.009 | 52% |

Read it carefully. At the **canonical post-earnings-drift horizon (one quarter)** the long-short
spread is **+0.21%** at **t = 0.42 / placebo p = 0.30** — indistinguishable from shuffling the
labels. The long leg ("up-revised stocks keep beating the market") beats SPY exactly **50%** of
the time: a **coin flip**, not a winning streak. A whisper of an effect only appears at the
**6-month** horizon (spread +1.45%, t = **1.98**) — and even there it *just misses* the desk's
**t ≥ 2** REAL bar, and (below) it does not survive costs.

## Costs — the gross whisper does not survive

Each quarter rebalances both legs (one-way 10 bps/leg × 4 crossings) plus a 50 bps/yr borrow on
the short, pro-rated to the hold.

| horizon | gross spread | gross *t* | net spread | net *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month (21d)  | +0.25% | 0.97 | **−0.20%** | −0.77 |
| 1-quarter (63d) | +0.21% | 0.42 | **−0.32%** | −0.65 |
| 2-quarter (126d) | +1.45% | 1.98 | **+0.80%** | 1.09 |

At the quarterly horizon the spread turns **negative** net of costs. Even the 6-month spread,
the only one with a gross *t* near 2, collapses to **t = 1.09** once you pay to trade it. There
is no horizon at which an *implementable* long-short revision book clears the bar.

## Robustness — the spread is flat-to-negative in the cut

| tercile cut | n quarters | 63d spread | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| top/bottom 20% | 98 | **−0.27%** | −0.41 | 0.693 |
| top/bottom 33% (headline) | 98 | +0.21% | 0.42 | 0.304 |
| top/bottom 40% | 98 | +0.53% | 1.20 | 0.073 |

Sharpening the cut to the *most* extreme up/down-revisions (top/bottom 20%) — where a real edge
should be *strongest* — makes the spread **negative**. The point estimate wobbles around zero
with the cut: the hallmark of noise, not signal.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, and a planted edge lights up

On a deterministic stock-quarter panel (40 names, 90 quarters) where forward return is built as
`edge · rev_score + noise`, the same tercile book + label-shuffle placebo recovers the truth:

| planted edge | n quarters | spread | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no edge) | 90 | +0.05% | **0.07** | 0.469 |
| **0.02** (modest) | 90 | +4.53% | **6.65** | 0.000 |
| **0.05** (large) | 90 | +11.26% | **16.14** | 0.000 |

With **no** planted edge the book sits at **t = 0.07** (no false positive — the machinery does
not manufacture a spread from noise). A modest planted link drives **t = 6.65** and the placebo
*p* to zero. The control proves the measurement engine is unbiased **and** that it would have
*easily* flagged a real revision edge of plausible size — so the real tape's quarterly **t =
0.42** is what an **absent** edge looks like, not an undetected one.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The proxy long-short spread is **+0.21% at the canonical quarterly horizon,
  t = 0.42, placebo p = 0.30**, and the long leg beats the market a flat **50%** of the time. A
  whisper appears only at 6 months (t = **1.98**) and even that **just misses the t ≥ 2 bar**.
  Decades of literature support the *existence* of a revision/PEAD effect, but our realized-proxy
  tape does **not** clear the desk's REAL bar ⇒ **WEAK**, not REAL. (Survivorship on the basket
  can only *flatter* this.)
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of 10 bps/leg one-way costs and a 50 bps/yr short borrow, the
  spread is **negative at 1 month (−0.20%) and at the quarter (−0.32%)**, and the only positive
  net horizon (6-month, +0.80%) carries **t = 1.09**. There is no implementable book here — the
  gross whisper is *exactly* the size of the trading frictions.
- **"Free lunch"? — BUSTED.** "Up-revised stocks keep beating the market" is a real *gross*
  tendency that **evaporates the moment you price execution** — a textbook factor-zoo mirage: an
  in-sample tilt that does not clear inference and does not survive costs.
